lines.text: - Not decided: what the tool does when the tracker lacks a type that a play must file. Initialize's approved page has the filing play "stop with a plain message that points to initialize", and the Must not of Orchestration is "Stop a person. Every gate has a way past it that records what's owed."
- Not decided: whether the pull requests are reached through this tool, or through a second tool for the code host.
- Not decided: whether the tool gives back each tracker's own fields, as the adapter does today ("the adapter does not normalize output across platforms"), or the same fields for every tracker.

- Not decided: where the tool lives: with Garura's tools, where ADR 065 records "the Agent-work tool, recorded as a feature", or in a component of its own for tools, as the direction of #620 (tools become a first-class Garura component) puts it.

- Not decided: how GitLab, Jira and Linear each hold a work item's type, its parent and its close reason. Today the adapter sets no type on GitLab ("GitLab has no issue types here."), links a parent there only as a related link, and drops the close reason there; it does not reach Jira or Linear. No approved source says what these trackers offer.
- Not decided: what the link is when the intents and the work are on two platforms, such as intents in Jira and work on GitHub.
- Not decided: which plays make the link: the plan plays for each epic, /start-change for an issue it files, the filing of a bug, or more than one of them.
- Not decided: which pieces of work hang straight under an intent: only an epic, as the way of working says, or also a piece of work that no epic holds, as Garura's own open work was moved in #1021.
- Not decided: how an epic that serves more than one intent hangs under each of them, since "an issue has only one parent."

- Not decided: whether a GitHub sub-issue may sit in a repository of another organization. The approved research says: "The docs do not say whether the other repository may be in another organization."
- Not decided: how GitLab, Jira and Linear each hold a parent link across projects. No approved source gives it; the approved research names only Jira's key written in the work.
- Not decided: where the list lives: on a memory shelf, as the direction of #620 puts the meanings, in a project setting, as #952 sorts the issue types, or inside the tool that knows the tracker.
- Not decided: which meaning of a Spike the list gives: a question to answer before a story can be built, as the way of working says, or a proof on something already built, as the ontology says.

- Not decided: how the list says a Business Intent, a Spike, a Chore and a Bug are marked: by their type with no label, as the way of working says, or with the label `product` on a Business Intent and the label `work-item` on a Spike, a Chore or a Bug, as the ontology says.
- Not decided: whether the list holds the type Feature, for a feature item in a plan, which Initialize's six types do not name.
- Not decided: what may stand in for an Epic or a Story in a tracker that cannot make them, since an Epic and a Story are marked by their type and "Neither has a label."
